title: Site reliability engineering
subtitle: A declared systemd fleet, tunnelled ingress, a documented Redis topology and written runbooks keep my estate recoverable.

stats.label: written runbooks, from startup to performance degradation
to roll back the registration lock that broke every client

lede: Auth and access plane holds the operations layer for my whole estate. As its only operator, I need the estate to start, fail and recover the same way every time, so the fleet is declared and versioned and startup order is a property of configuration. A few dozen services run under one systemd stack target. PartOf cascades carry a dependency's restart to its dependants, drop-ins make data-store clients wait for the network, and timers run routine work such as container cleanup. Unit files and a readable inventory are versioned with the code, so the fleet is rebuilt from source. AgentOS gets the same practice for its own releases.
quote: I reverse my own change when the evidence calls for it.
evidence: Site reliability engineering: a declared systemd fleet of a few dozen services under one stack target, with restart cascades and start order versioned with the code.
Incident response and runbooks: 8 written runbooks with thresholds, a severity model and escalation paths, and a registration lock that broke every client rolled back within 1 day.
Observability and alerting: Prometheus with file-based discovery of GPU nodes, Grafana dashboards and Alertmanager routing by severity to SMS paging.
Zero-trust and zero-inbound networking: public surfaces reached only through outbound tunnels and a private mesh, with 0 open inbound ports.
author: Corey James
